term:Continuous Monitoring.deep_dive: The always-on watch over deployed AI: performance and error patterns, data and concept drift, fairness metrics over time, security anomalies, and usage/reliance patterns — wired to thresholds, alerts, owners, and playbooks so detection produces action. It exists because AI degrades silently: models keep answering confidently as the world moves.
term:Continuous Monitoring.exam_tip: The EU AI Act makes post-market monitoring mandatory for high-risk systems — monitoring answers are compliance answers, not just hygiene.

term:Counterfactual Fairness.deep_dive: A causal fairness criterion: a decision is fair if it would remain the same in a counterfactual world where the individual's protected attribute differed but everything else causally consistent stayed equal. Conceptually elegant, practically demanding — it requires a causal model of how attributes influence features.
term:Counterfactual Fairness.exam_tip: Recognize it as an individual-level, causal fairness definition — contrast with group statistical metrics like demographic parity.

term:Data Acquisition.deep_dive: Obtaining data for AI — collection, purchase, licensing, scraping, or partnership — with governance gates at the door: legal rights to each source, terms permitting the intended use, provenance recording, and quality screening. Most training-data legal problems are acquisition problems discovered too late.
term:Data Acquisition.exam_tip: Possessing data ≠ having rights to train on it — the acquisition-stage rights check is the tested control.

term:Data Annotation.deep_dive: Attaching labels to raw data so supervised learning has ground truth — often via human labelers whose guidelines, consistency, and biases directly shape model behavior. Governance touches: labeling instructions as bias vectors, inter-annotator agreement as quality metric, and labor/sub-tier considerations in outsourced annotation.
term:Data Annotation.exam_tip: Label quality caps model quality — biased or inconsistent annotation is a root cause the exam expects you to trace.

term:Data Dependency.deep_dive: AI's defining reliance: system behavior is a function of the data it was trained and fed on, making data quality, representativeness, and availability first-order risk factors. Dependencies also chain — upstream source changes silently propagate into model behavior downstream.
term:Data Dependency.exam_tip: An ISO 23894 risk-source theme: when a scenario's model misbehaves, interrogate the data dependencies before the algorithm.

term:Data Drift.deep_dive: Production inputs drifting away from the training distribution — new demographics, changed formats, seasonal shifts — degrading performance even though the world's underlying input-output relationship holds. Statistical distribution monitoring catches it; retraining on current data remedies it.
term:Data Drift.exam_tip: Data drift = inputs change; concept drift = the relationship changes — pick precisely, the exam pairs them as distractors.

term:Data Governance.deep_dive: Managing data as a governed asset: lawful authority to use each source, quality dimensions measured, fitness-for-purpose verified, stewardship roles assigned, lineage recorded, and security applied across the pipeline. In AI it is the upstream half of model governance — most model failures are data failures with a delay.
term:Data Governance.exam_tip: The EU AI Act makes data governance an explicit high-risk requirement (training/validation/testing data quality and relevance) — it's law, not just practice.

term:Data Integrity.deep_dive: Assurance that data is accurate, complete, and unaltered except through authorized change — spanning accidental corruption and deliberate tampering (data poisoning being the AI-specific attack). Controls: validation checks, access restriction, versioning, checksums, and tamper-evident logging.
term:Data Integrity.exam_tip: Poisoned training data is an integrity failure with model-wide blast radius — integrity controls on training pipelines are security controls.

term:Data Lineage.deep_dive: The recorded journey of data from source through every transformation, join, filter, and feature-engineering step to the training set — the data's biography. It answers the incident question ('what fed this model?'), the audit question ('prove it'), and the rights question ('whose data is in here?').
term:Data Lineage.exam_tip: Lineage = the journey; provenance = the origin — the definitional split is a reliable test item.

term:Data Provenance.deep_dive: The origin story of data: source, collection method, date, legal terms, and consent status — recorded at acquisition because it cannot be reconstructed later. Provenance underwrites every downstream claim: lawful training data, honored licenses, defensible deletion, and credible audits.
term:Data Provenance.exam_tip: Provenance = origin; lineage = journey through transformations — paired and tested together.

term:Data Quality Review.deep_dive: The structured checkpoint assessing data against quality dimensions — accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness — before it trains anything. Reviews recur: quality decays as sources evolve, so gates belong at acquisition, pre-training, and periodically in production pipelines.
term:Data Quality Review.exam_tip: Sequencing: quality review precedes training — discovering data problems via model misbehavior means the gate was missing.

term:Data Sheet.deep_dive: Datasheets for datasets: standardized documentation covering motivation, composition, collection process, preprocessing, recommended and discouraged uses — the dataset's spec sheet, by analogy to electronic components. Paired with model cards, they form the documentation backbone of accountable AI.
term:Data Sheet.exam_tip: Datasheet documents a dataset; model card documents a model; system card documents the deployed assembly — match precisely.

term:Deactivation Policy.deep_dive: The predefined rulebook for turning AI systems off: triggers (risk thresholds breached, regulation changed, performance decayed, vendor sunset), authority to invoke, decommissioning procedure, data disposition, and stakeholder notice. Its existence converts retirement from emergency improvisation into a governed decision.
term:Deactivation Policy.exam_tip: Mature-practice marker: the organization decided *in advance* when and how systems die — exam scenarios reward predefined triggers.

term:Decommissioning.deep_dive: The operational teardown of an AI system: executing the retirement plan — dependency wind-down, successor cutover, access and credential revocation, data return/deletion per obligations, artifact archival, and monitoring shutdown, with records preserved beyond the system's death. Verification closes it: confirming nothing still silently depends on the corpse.
term:Decommissioning.exam_tip: Records outlive the system — EU AI Act documentation retention continues after decommissioning; 'delete everything at shutdown' is wrong.

term:Deployment.deep_dive: The lifecycle transition from artifact to operation: releasing a validated system into production through a chosen strategy (canary, phased, shadow, blue-green), with monitoring live from minute one and rollback criteria pre-agreed. Governance-wise it's a formal gate: named approvers, documented go/no-go, and change management for the humans affected.
term:Deployment.exam_tip: Deployment is a decision with an audit trail, not an event — scenarios reward staged strategies and pre-defined rollback over big-bang launches.

term:Documentation and Reporting.deep_dive: The evidence layer of governance: contemporaneous records of decisions, tests, approvals, incidents, and changes, plus the reporting flows that keep oversight bodies informed — internal (committees, boards) and external (regulators, auditors). Its absence converts good governance into unprovable governance.
term:Documentation and Reporting.exam_tip: 'If it isn't documented, it didn't happen' — in audit and enforcement scenarios, the documented-but-imperfect program beats the perfect-but-undocumented one.

term:External Communication Plan.deep_dive: The prepared playbook for speaking about AI beyond the organization: user transparency notices, regulator communications, incident disclosures, and press response — with speakers, approval chains, and pre-cleared facts defined before a crisis compresses timelines. Improvised AI-incident messaging reliably compounds the incident.
term:External Communication Plan.exam_tip: Incident scenarios reward pre-planned communications with designated owners — 'draft a statement after containment' is table stakes, having the plan already is the answer.

term:Fairness.deep_dive: The principle that AI treats individuals and groups equitably — operationalized through competing mathematical definitions (parity, equalized odds, calibration) that cannot all hold simultaneously, forcing documented context-specific choices. It spans process (how decisions are made) and outcome (who gets what).
term:Fairness.exam_tip: The mature answer acknowledges metric trade-offs and picks per context with documentation — 'optimize all fairness metrics' is mathematically impossible.

term:Feedback Loop.deep_dive: Model outputs shaping the future inputs the model learns from: predictive policing directing patrols that generate arrest data justifying more patrols; recommenders training users whose clicks retrain recommenders. Loops entrench and amplify initial bias, and they hide from static testing — only longitudinal monitoring sees them.
term:Feedback Loop.exam_tip: Feedback loops explain how a small initial bias becomes structural — cite them in scenarios where deployment data feeds retraining.

term:Fine-Tuning.deep_dive: Adapting a pretrained model with additional domain-specific training — the economic default for LLM deployment. Governance inheritance is the catch: the fine-tuned model carries the base model's biases, memorized data, and licensing constraints, plus whatever the new data adds — and substantial modification can shift regulatory roles from deployer toward provider.
term:Fine-Tuning.exam_tip: Fine-tuning inherits base-model risk and can transfer provider obligations — two consequences in one technique.

term:Fit-for-Purpose.deep_dive: The proportionality test for data and systems: quality is not absolute but relative to the intended use — clinical decision support demands a different evidentiary bar than playlist ranking. Fit-for-purpose evaluation asks whether this data, this model, these controls suffice for this use and its stakes.
term:Fit-for-Purpose.exam_tip: Anti-perfectionism principle with teeth: the question is never 'is the data perfect' but 'is it adequate for this purpose' — proportionality is the tested logic.
